name: Make.com
description: Connect your own Make.com account to view and run your automation scenarios directly from Webbee -- see scenario status, run one on demand, and control activation, all via your own Make API token.

tools.name: connect_make
tools.description: Connect Make.com by saving your own API token, after checking it actually works. Create the token in Make: avatar (bottom-left) -> Profile -> API tab -> Add token. The account's zone (eu1/eu2/us1/us2) is auto-detected -- you don't need to know it.

api_token.description: Make.com API token -- create it in Make: avatar (bottom-left) -> Profile -> API tab -> Add token.
api_token.title: Api Token

tools.name: disconnect_make
tools.description: Disconnect Make.com: deletes the saved API token and zone. Existing scenarios in your Make account are never touched.

tools.name: get_make_connection
tools.description: Check whether Make.com is currently connected (does not reveal the saved token).

tools.name: list_make_teams
tools.description: List the Make.com teams your connected account belongs to. Needed once to pick which team's scenarios to show -- Make requires a specific team (or organization) scope, it has no single global scenario list.

tools.name: select_team
tools.description: Pick which Make.com team's scenarios to show. Run list_make_teams first to see the available team ids. This is a standing choice -- it stays selected until changed again.

team_id.description: Make team id to scope scenario listing to (see list_make_teams).
team_id.title: Team Id

tools.name: list_scenarios
tools.description: List your Make.com scenarios for the selected team -- name, active/paused/invalid state, and last edit time. Run connect_make and select_team first if you haven't yet.

tools.name: run_scenario
tools.description: Run one of your Make.com scenarios right now, by scenario_id (see list_scenarios). This executes the scenario's real actions in Make immediately -- sending emails, writing to connected apps, etc. There is no dry-run or undo, so this always asks for confirm=true first.

scenario_id.description: Make scenario id to run now (see list_scenarios).
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

confirm.description: Must be true. Running a scenario executes its real actions in Make right now (sending emails, writing to connected apps, etc.) -- there is no dry-run or undo.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: set_scenario_active
tools.description: Activate (turn on/schedule) or deactivate (pause) a Make.com scenario by scenario_id (see list_scenarios). Reversible -- flip it back any time -- so unlike run_scenario this needs no confirmation.

scenario_id.description: Make scenario id to activate/deactivate (see list_scenarios).
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

active.description: True to activate (schedule/turn on) the scenario, False to deactivate (pause) it.
active.title: Active

tools.name: set_outgoing_webhook
tools.description: Save (or clear, with an empty webhook_url) the Make Custom Webhook trigger URL that send_webhook_event will POST to. Get this URL by adding a 'Custom Webhook' module as the first step of a Make scenario and copying its URL. This is independent of connect_make.

webhook_url.description: The Custom Webhook trigger URL copied from a Make scenario (add a 'Custom Webhook' module, copy its URL). Leave empty to remove/disable it.
webhook_url.title: Webhook Url

tools.name: get_outgoing_webhook_status
tools.description: Check whether an outgoing Make webhook URL is configured (does not reveal the URL itself).

tools.name: send_webhook_event
tools.description: Send an event payload to the configured Make webhook right now -- for other Imperal apps/automations to trigger a Make scenario. Run set_outgoing_webhook first if you haven't configured one yet.

payload.description: JSON-serializable payload to POST to the configured Make webhook URL -- shape is whatever the receiving Make scenario expects.
payload.title: Payload

tools.name: get_scenario_blueprint
tools.description: Read a scenario's actual module list (blueprint) -- what each numbered step in the flow is and does, in the same order the Make editor numbers them. This is how to answer 'what is module N' or 'what does the Nth step do'.

draft.description: True for the draft (unsaved editor) version, False for the live/published version. Omit to get Make's own default for this scenario.
draft.title: Draft

BlueprintModule.description:
One module (step) in a scenario's blueprint -- position, app/module
identity, and a short label describing what it is. `position` is
1-based to match how modules are numbered in the Make editor UI, so
'module 7' means the 7th entry here.
BlueprintModule.title: BlueprintModule

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List the app connections in your Make team -- what a scenario's modules actually authenticate as (which account/app each connection is for, and whether it's about to expire).

tools.name: delete_connection
tools.description: Permanently delete a Make connection. Any scenario using it will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Any scenario using this connection will stop working once it's deleted.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: rename_connection
tools.description: Rename a Make connection's display name.

name.description: New display name for the connection.
name.title: Name

tools.name: verify_connection
tools.description: Test whether a Make connection's credentials still work.

tools.name: list_data_stores
tools.description: List the data stores (Make's own key/value storage) in your team, with record counts and size.

tools.name: create_data_store
tools.description: Create a new Make data store (key/value storage a scenario can read/write).

name.description: Name for the new data store.
name.title: Name

data_structure_id.description: Optional data structure id defining the record schema. Omit for a schema-less store.
data_structure_id.title: Data Structure Id

tools.name: delete_data_store
tools.description: Permanently delete a Make data store and all of its records.

confirm.description: Must be true. This permanently deletes all its records.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: list_hooks
tools.description: List the incoming webhooks/mailhooks (Make 'hooks') in your team -- the triggers scenarios listen on, with their URL and whether they're enabled.

tools.name: set_hook_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a Make hook (incoming webhook/mailhook) without deleting it.

enabled.description: True to enable (accept data), False to disable.
enabled.title: Enabled

tools.name: delete_hook
tools.description: Permanently remove a Make hook. Any scenario using it will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Any scenario using this hook will stop working once it's deleted.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: list_incomplete_executions
tools.description: List a scenario's incomplete executions (failed runs held for manual resolution instead of being discarded) -- what failed, when, and whether it's already resolved.

scenario_id.description: Scenario id whose incomplete executions to list.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

status.description: Filter by derived status: resolved, scheduled, inprogress, or unresolved.
status.title: Status

tools.name: retry_incomplete_execution
tools.description: Retry one incomplete (failed) scenario execution after fixing the underlying issue.

tools.name: delete_incomplete_executions
tools.description: Permanently delete one scenario's incomplete executions -- explicit ids, or all=true with confirm=true to clear every one.

scenario_id.description: Scenario id whose incomplete executions to delete.
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

dlq_ids.description: Explicit incomplete execution ids to delete. Omit and set all=true to delete every one.
dlq_ids.title: Dlq Ids

all.description: Delete every incomplete execution of this scenario.
all.title: All

tools.name: bulk_set_scenario_active
tools.description: Activate or deactivate SEVERAL Make scenarios in one call by explicit scenario ids.

scenario_ids.description: Explicit Make scenario ids; 1-100, never inferred.
scenario_ids.title: Scenario Ids

active.description: True to activate every listed scenario, False to deactivate.
active.title: Active

tools.name: bulk_run_scenarios
tools.description: Run SEVERAL Make scenarios right now, by explicit scenario ids. Executes real actions in each scenario immediately -- no dry-run, always requires confirm=true.

scenario_ids.description: Explicit Make scenario ids; 1-100, never inferred.
scenario_ids.title: Scenario Ids

confirm.description: Must be true. Runs every listed scenario's real actions right now, with no dry-run or undo.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: bulk_delete_connections
tools.description: Permanently delete SEVERAL Make connections at once, by explicit connection ids. Any scenario using one will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Scenarios using these connections will stop working.
confirm.title: Confirm

tools.name: bulk_delete_hooks
tools.description: Permanently remove SEVERAL Make hooks at once, by explicit hook ids. Any scenario using one will stop working once it's gone.

confirm.description: Must be true. Scenarios using these hooks will stop working.
confirm.title: Confirm

secrets.name: make_api_token
secrets.description: Your own Make.com API token, from Make: avatar (bottom-left) -> Profile -> API tab -> Add token.

secrets.name: make_zone
secrets.description: Auto-detected Make.com account zone (eu1/eu2/us1/us2) -- set automatically by connect_make, not entered manually.

secrets.name: make_webhook_url
secrets.description: Outgoing Make Custom Webhook trigger URL (from a Make scenario's Custom Webhook module) -- send_webhook_event POSTs to this. Independent of the make_api_token connection above.

panels.title: How to get a Make API token
